title: promote-latest treats a zero-byte promotion record as no record, then dies with EEXIST at the record write
description: Found by the LCLI-638 reviewer (opum-workflow:reviewer at 2b97082c, finding 5, informational and pre-existing: the `!existing` logic is untouched by that commit). main() step 4 reads the record as `await readFile(args.recordPath, 'utf8').catch(() => null)`. A zero-byte file reads as the empty string, which is falsy, so it is treated as NO record at all: the run takes the fresh path, never applies the LCLI-638 resume gate, and then dies at the record write, `writeFile(recordPath, ..., { flag: 'wx' })`, with an uncaught EEXIST -- mapped by the entrypoint to exit 2 with a raw Node stack and no remedy. Measured end to end by the reviewer with a real record file and --promote: no registry write happens before the throw. An empty record is a plausible operator state (an interrupted first write, a touched file), and today it is indistinguishable from 'this is a fresh run' until the confusing failure. The distinction is worth making because the two states have opposite remedies: a missing record means promote normally; an empty one means the first run may have started and written nothing, so the operator needs to look before re-running.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A zero-byte promotion record refuses with a message naming the path and the empty-record state, before any registry write, on --dry-run and --promote alike, and exits 1 rather than dying with an uncaught EEXIST
A MISSING record still takes the fresh path exactly as before, and a test holds the two states apart (an empty file and an absent file do not produce the same behaviour)
bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change

plan: 1. Distinguish a zero-byte promotion record from an absent one at the step-4 read in scripts/promote-latest.mjs (readFile(...).catch(()=>null) treats "" as no record).
2. Refuse a zero-byte record before any registry write, naming the path and the empty-record state, on --dry-run and --promote alike, exit 1 (not the uncaught EEXIST at the wx write).
3. Keep the missing-record fresh path exactly as before, and add a test holding an empty file and an absent file apart (different behaviour).
4. bun test and bun run lore check exit 0.
implementationNotes: Claimed on branch fix/LCLI-641-zero-byte-record; implement-assignment will edit scripts/ and test/ only.

Implemented in scripts/promote-latest.mjs step 4: a present-but-empty promotion record (zero-byte or whitespace-only) now refuses with exit 1, naming the path and the empty-record state, before any registry write, on --dry-run and --promote alike. Absent (null) keeps the fresh path unchanged. Test in test/promote-latest.test.ts holds the two states apart. Gates: bun test 5000/2/0, bun run lore check exit 0, lint/typecheck exit 0. PR opum-ai/lore-cli#551.
finalSummary:
Delivered in opum-ai/lore-cli#551, code head 40bc4000, CI run 38179782047 on that SHA: 13 success, 1 skipped (`promotion is manual`, skipped by design on every dev PR), 0 failure, every required dev context green. The tracker-only closure commit rides the same PR; the merge gate is the run on the final pushed head.

WHAT LANDED. `scripts/promote-latest.mjs` main() step 4 now distinguishes a PRESENT-but-EMPTY promotion record from an ABSENT one. Absent (ENOENT -> `null`) keeps the fresh path unchanged, byte for byte. Present-but-empty (zero-byte or whitespace-only) refuses with exit 1, naming the path and the empty-record state, before any registry write, on `--dry-run` and `--promote` alike (the guard sits before the `--dry-run` branch). It no longer reaches `writeFile(..., { flag: "wx" })`, which threw an uncaught EEXIST that the entrypoint mapped to exit 2 with a raw stack and no remedy. Guard: `existing !== null && existing.trim() === ""`. The empty file is left in place -- deleting it is the deliberate act that means "start fresh".

TEST (test/promote-latest.test.ts) holds the two states apart: zero-byte on `--promote` and on `--dry-run`, and whitespace-only, each refused with exit 1, a message naming the path and "exists but is EMPTY", `w.writes` empty and the file left in place; absent exits 0, records every prior and promotes.

AC POSITIONS. AC1 (zero-byte refuses, naming path and state, before any registry write, both modes, exit 1) -- the new test asserts exactly that for all three cases. AC2 (missing record unchanged) -- the same test asserts the absent path exits 0, writes the record and prints "Recorded every prior latest to <path> before moving anything.". AC3 (bun test and bun run lore check exit 0; a reviewer pass covers the scripts/ change) -- bun test 5000 pass / 2 skip / 0 fail; bun run lore check exit 0; the scripts/ change is covered by the independent reviewer pass recorded against this head.

GATES, all measured: bun test 5000/2/0; bun run lore check exit 0 (the single warning is the pre-existing implementation.toml agent-profile-capacity warning, LCLI-662 residual, unrelated); bun run lint exit 0 (the 11 warnings + 1 info dev already carries); bun run typecheck exit 0. Mutation controls, both reddening exactly the one new case: removing the guard reproduced the exact EEXIST at the flag:"wx" write; narrowing to `existing === ""` left a whitespace-only record throwing an uncaught SyntaxError -- which is why the guard uses `.trim()`.
